# pnv (Rust)

> A Rust crate and `pnv` command for encrypted secrets in YAML that you commit. Values are
> AES-256-GCM encrypted `SECRET;v1:` tokens in plain-text YAML; only the symmetric key lives outside
> the repo. The crate decrypts the YAML in a build script (`pnv::build::Build`) or at run time
> (`pnv::Env`). It reads and writes the same keys, tokens and `.pnvrc` as the Dart `pnv` tool.
>
> This file is for an AI agent working in a Rust repo that uses pnv. `README.md` is the human
> version. Everything below was checked against `src/` and by running the command, not copied from
> the README; where they disagree, trust this file and fix the README.

pnv is a **library first**. The command is behind the default `cli` feature. A build script wants
`pnv = { version = "0.1", default-features = false }` under `[build-dependencies]`.

The command has init, create key, create/delete flavor, encrypt, decrypt, generate env and verify.
For set, get and show, use the Dart tool (`dart/`): the files are the same.

---

## The model, in one pass

```
  pnv create key            ──►  a key string. NEVER in the repo.
                                    │
  config/app.production.yaml        │            committed. secrets are ciphertext.
    database:
      url: SECRET;v1:<b64>   ◄──────┤ written by the Dart tool (pnv set / encrypt)
                                    │
     ┌──────────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────┐
     ▼ build.rs: Build::new(file).emit()                        ▼ run time: Env::load(file)
  cargo:rustc-env=DATABASE_URL=...                          env.get("DATABASE_URL")
  src: env!("DATABASE_URL")                                 values live only in memory
```

A **flavor** is a named key plus the file-name suffix that selects it. `app.production.yaml` is
flavor `production`; `local.yaml` is `local`. A `.pnvrc` (JSON, written by the Dart tool) names the
key `storage` directory and the flavors, each with optional alias suffixes:
`{"storage":"keys","flavors":{"production":["ci"]}}`. Flavor `production` has the key file
`<storage>/production.key`, and `app.ci.yaml` also uses it.

---

## Finding the key

One lookup serves `Env::load`, `Build` and `pnv verify`. The first match wins:

1. `PNV_KEY_<FLAVOR>` in the environment: flavor in capitals, `-` turned into `_`
   (`staging-eu` ⇒ `PNV_KEY_STAGING_EU`). Trimmed; blank counts as unset. Needs no `.pnvrc`.
2. `<storage>/<flavor>.key` from the nearest `.pnvrc`, found by walking up from the current
   directory. The `.pnvrc` is loaded only when this step is reached.
3. For each flavor that lists the name as an alias, in file order: its variable, then its key file.

Nothing found ⇒ `Error::KeyNotFound`; nothing to look up ⇒ `Error::NoKey`.
In code: `KeyLookup::new().file(path)` (or `.flavor(..)`, `.key_file(..)`, `.key(..)`) then
`.resolve()` ⇒ `ResolvedKey { key, source, flavor }`.

On a build server, set `PNV_KEY_<FLAVOR>` and ship no key file.

---

## Build script

```toml
[build-dependencies]
pnv = { version = "0.1", default-features = false }
```

```rust
// build.rs
fn main() {
    pnv::build::Build::new("app.production.yaml")   // path from the package root
        .emit()
        .unwrap_or_else(|err| panic!("{err}"));
}
// src/main.rs
const DATABASE_URL: &str = env!("DATABASE_URL");
```

`.flavor("x")` overrides the flavor, `.key_file(path)` reads the key from a file, `.instructions()`
returns the lines instead of printing them. `emit` prints, in this order:

- `cargo:rerun-if-changed=<yaml>`, then the `.pnvrc` and the key file when they were used
- `cargo:rerun-if-env-changed=PNV_KEY_<FLAVOR>` for every variable the lookup read
- `cargo:rustc-env=NAME=value` per value, in file order

Values are plain text: strings unquoted, null empty, a float as Dart writes it (`1e3` ⇒ `1000.0`).
`env!` gives a `&str`, so parse numbers yourself. Nothing is printed unless every value can be
passed on.

Failures to know:

- **A value holding a line break** (a PEM key, a multi-line string) ⇒ `Error::LineBreak`. Cargo takes
  one instruction per line. Read that file at run time with `Env::load`.
- **A key name that is empty or holds `=`, NUL or a line break** ⇒ `Error::InvalidEnvName`.
- **Secrets are readable in the output.** They are compiled into the binary and kept under
  `target/`. Do not treat a built binary as secret-free.

---

## Run time

```rust
let env = pnv::Env::load("config/app.production.yaml")?;   // key found as above
let url = env.get("DATABASE_URL");                          // Option<&Value>
```

`Env::read(path, &key)` and `Env::parse(yaml, &key)` take a `Key`
(`Key::decode(&str)`). `env.to_dotenv()` is byte for byte what the Dart `pnv generate env` writes.
Nested keys flatten with `_` and upper-case (`db.host` ⇒ `DB_HOST`); a list ⇒ `Error::UnsupportedType`;
a top level that is not a map ⇒ `Error::NotAMap`. When two keys flatten to the same name, the later
wins. Nothing is written to the process environment, on purpose.

`Value` is `String | Int | Float | Bool | Null`, by the YAML 1.2 core schema. A decrypted secret is
always a `String`. `Value` is `Display`.

Also public: `encrypt(&str, &Key)`, `decrypt(&str, &Key)`, `is_secret`, `create_key`,
`write_key_file`, `Pnvrc`, `flavor_from_path`, `key_env_var`, `verify`, `suspect_plaintext`.

---

## Command

Never prompts; every input is a flag. Exit 0 on success, 1 on any error (bad flags too, not 2).
Errors go to stderr as `❌ <message>`. KEY = `-k, --key <key>` | `-f, --key-file <path>` |
`--flavor <name>` (env `PNV_KEY_<FLAVOR>` is checked first, as in the lookup above).
Global: `--quiet` (errors + requested output only), `--loud` (every step; wins over --quiet).

```
pnv init [-s <storage>] [-f <flavor>]... [--gitignore]  .pnvrc here or nearest above; never replaces a key
pnv create key                                          prints a new key (one line, base64)
pnv create flavor -n <name> [--force]                   refuses existing flavor or key file without --force
pnv delete flavor -n <name>... --force                  refuses without --force; unknown name deletes nothing
pnv encrypt|enc|e|encode [KEY] <value>...               one SECRET;v1: token per line
pnv decrypt|dec|d|decode [KEY] <token>...               one value per line; checks the key id
pnv generate env (-i <x.yaml> | -d <dir>) [-o outputs] [KEY]
                                                        <output>/<stem>.env, all rendered before any write
pnv verify [-d, --directory <envs>]                     exit 0 clean, exit 1 problems
```

`init` storage defaults to `~/.<project dir name>`; it adopts `*.key` files already in storage.
`generate env`: with KEY, one key for every file; without, each file's flavor comes from its name.
`--flavor` + `-d` keeps only that flavor's group; a flavor not in an existing `.pnvrc` is an error.

`pnv verify` needs a `.pnvrc` at or above the current directory, else it prints
`No .pnvrc found. Run `pnv init` first.` and exits 1. It walks `.yaml`/`.yml` under the directory (default: the `.pnvrc` directory),
skipping `.git`, `target`, `build`, `node_modules`, `.dart_tool`, and reports a secret that does not
decrypt with its flavor's key, a plaintext value that looks like a secret, and a key `storage`
directory inside the project. A file needs a key only if it holds a secret.

---

## What must never be committed

- The key files and the `PNV_KEY_*` values.
- Safe to commit: `.pnvrc`, the encrypted `*.yaml`.

## Source map

| Where to look | For |
| --- | --- |
| `src/main.rs`, `src/cli/` | the command |
| `src/build.rs` | `Build` and the cargo instructions |
| `src/lookup.rs` | `KeyLookup`, the key search order |
| `src/env.rs`, `src/loader.rs` | `Env`, YAML ⇒ values |
| `src/token.rs`, `src/key.rs` | the `SECRET;` format, keys |
| `src/pnvrc.rs`, `src/flavor.rs` | `.pnvrc`, flavors, `PNV_KEY_` names |
| `src/verify.rs`, `src/detector.rs` | `pnv verify` |
| `../spec/format.md`, `../spec/vectors/` | the shared contract both tools pass |
| `examples/build-script/` | a crate that runs the build-script recipe |
